rv.q: It’s a roundly well-acted and sophisticated evening that offers plenty of light delight while seriously considering a marriage rerouted not by a seven-year itch but a 15-year switch.
Laura Wade’s incisive reworking cuts to the continually relevant themes of W Somerset Maugham’s crisp comedy of marital manners
Beautifully acted by the entire cast, directed with finesse and flair, it’s a lovely soufflé of feeling and humour, a theatrical treat as stylish and well-judged as the interiors Constance designs.
It all makes for a delightfully entertaining evening out, full of sparklingly sharp yet subtle satire which feels just as relevant now as it did a century ago.
An excellent production of a timeless play, brought smartly to life by a neat adaptation.

cn.t: Laura Wade's sharp adaptation of Maugham's 1926 comedy feels surprisingly modern, with critics praising its witty satire of gender roles and marriage. Rose Leslie leads this sparkling revival that suggests Maugham deserves reassessment.
